description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Communication Systems topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: communication-systems

facts.claim: Carrier amplitude varies with the message

source.quote: the instantaneous amplitude of the wave is varied in proportion to that of the message signal

facts.claim: Standard AM has sidebands on both sides of the carrier

source.quote: the standard method produces sidebands on either side of the carrier frequency

facts.claim: AM bandwidth is twice the highest message frequency

source.quote: Amplitude modulation produces an output signal the bandwidth of which is twice the maximum frequency of the original baseband signal

facts.claim: SSB saves bandwidth and carrier power

source.quote: Single-sideband modulation avoids this bandwidth increase, and the power wasted on a carrier

facts.claim: FM varies the instantaneous frequency with the message

source.quote: a carrier wave is varied in its instantaneous frequency in proportion to a property

facts.claim: Digital FM is frequency-shift keying

source.quote: a form of frequency modulation known as frequency-shift keying (FSK)

facts.claim: Carson's rule: B ≈ 2(Δf + fm)

source.quote: the Carson's bandwidth rule defines the approximate bandwidth requirements

facts.claim: Uses peak frequency deviation and highest modulating frequency

source.quote: is the peak frequency deviation

facts.claim: White noise has a flat (uniform) power spectral density

source.quote: White refers to the idea that it has uniform power spectral density across the frequency band

facts.claim: Gaussian: normal distribution with zero mean

source.quote: Gaussian because it has a normal distribution in the time domain with an average time domain value of zero

facts.claim: PAM has been largely replaced by pulse-code modulation

source.quote: non-baseband applications having been largely replaced by pulse-code modulation

facts.claim: DPCM encodes changes between consecutive samples

source.quote: encodes changes between consecutive samples of a signal, rather than the signal's value directly

facts.claim: Both ends predict the value from the previous signal

source.quote: Both the transmitter and the receiver make an estimate or prediction of the signal's value

facts.claim: Time divided into recurring fixed time slots, one per channel

source.quote: The time domain is divided into several recurrent time slots of fixed length, one for each sub-channel

facts.claim: T1 carries 24 channels at 1.544 Mbit/s

source.quote: The discrete signals on the trunk line carried 1.544 Mbit/s

facts.claim: The matched filter maximises SNR

source.quote: The matched filter is the optimal linear filter for maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio

facts.claim: Correlates a known template with the received signal

source.quote: correlating a known delayed signal, or template, with an unknown signal

facts.claim: ISI: one symbol interferes with later symbols

source.quote: one symbol interferes with subsequent symbols

facts.claim: Countered by equalisation (and pulse shaping)

source.quote: Ways to alleviate intersymbol interference include adaptive equalization

facts.claim: PSK changes the phase of a constant-frequency carrier

source.quote: conveys data by changing (modulating) the phase of a constant frequency carrier wave

facts.claim: Digital modulation uses a finite set of distinct signals

source.quote: Any digital modulation scheme uses a finite number of distinct signals to represent digital data

facts.claim: SNR = signal power / noise power, often in dB

source.quote: SNR is defined as the ratio of signal power to noise power, often expressed in decibels
